check_service_status.description: Check whether On This Day is answering, and how quickly. This is the one action that reports a problem as a value instead of failing the step, so a workflow can decide what to do about it. Being asked to slow down is reported separately from being down. No API key required.

mock_response.message: On This Day is up and serving Wikipedia's day-of-the-year data.

check_service_status.name: check_service_status

online.description: Whether the service answered with usable day-of-the-year data.

rate_limited.description: Whether it asked this workspace to slow down.

reachable.description: Whether it answered at all. A service that is reachable but not online is refusing or misreporting rather than down.

response_time_ms.description: How long the answer took, in milliseconds.

status_code.description: The HTTP status it answered with, or empty when it could not be reached.

get_anniversaries.description: Find what turns fifty, a hundred or two hundred today: the entries on a date whose age this year divides exactly by the interval you set. The service publishes a year and never a distance from one, so this is arithmetic it cannot do. Biggest anniversary first. No API key required.

parameters.description: The day of the year to look up, as a date: 2026-02-02, 2/2 or February 2 all work. Any year in it is ignored, because the service is keyed on a month and a day: asking about 2026-02-02 returns everything that ever happened on a 2 February. Leave empty to use today, or to use the month and day fields below.

description: Look up what happened on any day of the year with On This Day, the free keyless API behind byabbe.se. Get the events, births and deaths Wikipedia records for a date, today's unless you name another, narrowed by keyword or by century, pick one at random for a fact-of-the-day post, or find what turns fifty or a hundred today. Every year comes back as a number rather than the string the service sends, BC years included, and a date with an empty section is an empty answer rather than a failed step. The data is harvested from Wikipedia and shares its CC BY-SA 3.0 licence. No account and no API key: connecting takes one click.
